proofs.proof_tex:
Fix a member of \(\mathfrak M\).  Put \(a_-=\inf_{\beta\in\mathcal K}a(\beta)>0\), and also fix one \(\beta_0\in\mathcal K\).  We treat separately diverging and bounded main-wave subsequences.

First suppose \(N\to\infty\).  Define
\[
q_n(\beta)=E_{S_m}\inf_{H\in\mathcal H_T}
N\{V_T(H,\beta)-V_T(G_T(\beta),\beta)\},
\qquad T=T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}.
\tag{28}
\]
By \(\mathrm{prop{:}first\text{-}order\text{-}arbitrary\text{-}action\text{-}optimality}\), there is \(\epsilon_n\downarrow0\) such that
\(\inf_{\beta\in\mathcal K}q_n(\beta)\geq-\epsilon_n\).  Conditional independence of the pilot and main outcomes and the exact reduction give
\[
n\{R_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta)-R_n^{\mathrm{or}}(\beta)\}
\geq nD_{n,m}(\beta)-\frac Nn\epsilon_n.
\tag{29}
\]
Here \(N=o(n)\), so \(m/n\to1\).  The macroscopic deletion limit in \(\mathrm{thm{:}oracle\text{-}deletion\text{-}loss}\) therefore gives
\[
\sup_{\beta\in\mathcal K}|nD_{n,m}(\beta)-a(\beta)|\longrightarrow0.
\tag{30}
\]
Equations (29)--(30) imply, uniformly over all pilot rules and all \(\beta\),
\[
R_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta)-R_n^{\mathrm{or}}(\beta)
\geq\frac{a_-}{2n}
\tag{31}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\).

Now suppose that \(N\) is bounded along a subsequence.  Combining the two main-oracle terms in \(\mathrm{thm{:}exact\text{-}ht\text{-}accounting}\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
R_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta_0)-R_n^{\mathrm{or}}(\beta_0)
&=d_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}(\beta_0)\\
&\quad+\left(\frac Nn\right)^2E\!\left[
V_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\delta_m,\beta_0)
-V_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(0,\beta_0)
\right].
\end{aligned}
\tag{32}
\]
Every risk is nonnegative.  The fixed-member moment envelope and \(\mathrm{lem{:}uniform\text{-}single\text{-}wave\text{-}risk}\) give \(V_T(0,\beta_0)\leq C/N\).  Hence
\[
R_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta_0)-R_n^{\mathrm{or}}(\beta_0)
\geq d_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}(\beta_0)-C\frac N{n^2}.
\tag{33}
\]
Since \(n d_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}(\beta_0)\to a(\beta_0)>0\) by \(\mathrm{thm{:}oracle\text{-}deletion\text{-}loss}\) and bounded \(N\) makes the second term in (33) \(o(n^{-1})\), the right side is at least \(a(\beta_0)/(2n)\) for all sufficiently large indices of this subsequence.

Every subsequence of a nonnegative integer sequence \(N\) has a further subsequence on which \(N\) is bounded or \(N\to\infty\).  Thus (31)--(33) imply that some constant \(c_0>0\), depending only on the fixed member and \(\beta_0\), satisfies, eventually,
\[
\inf_{\delta_m}\sup_{\beta\in\mathcal K}
\left[R_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta)-R_n^{\mathrm{or}}(\beta)\right]_+
\geq\frac{c_0}{n}.
\tag{34}
\]
The left side is \(\mathcal E_n(m)\).  Multiplying (34) by \(n^{3/2}\) proves exactly the claimed nearly-all-pilot divergence.

added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix one member of \(\mathfrak M\), and condition throughout on its deterministic complete baseline array.  Write
\[
w_q=2^{1-K_f}c_q,
\qquad
\mu_{iq}(\beta)=E_\beta\{Y_{in}(q)\mid x_{in}\},
\qquad
\varepsilon_{iq}=Y_{in}(q)-\mu_{iq}(\beta).
\tag{1}
\]
The first and second conditional moments in (1) are continuous and uniformly bounded on \(\mathcal X\times\mathcal K\) by \(\mathrm{ass{:}arraywise\text{-}moment\text{-}regularity}\), and different units are independent by \(\mathrm{ass{:}stable\text{-}product\text{-}law}\).

We first record the regularity of a uniform complement.  If \(h_{in}(\beta)\) is any coordinate or product of coordinates among \(x_{in}\) and \(\{\mu_{iq}(\beta):q\in\mathcal Q\}\), boundedness and the variance identity for sampling without replacement give
\[
E_{S_m}\left|
\frac1N\sum_{i\in T}h_{in}(\beta)
-\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^nh_{in}(\beta)
\right|^2
\leq \frac{C_h}{N}.
\tag{2}
\]
Indeed, the left side is \((N^{-1}-n^{-1})\) times the finite-population variance of the bounded array, and that variance is at most a constant depending only on the fixed member.  Uniform continuity on the compact set \(\mathcal X\times\mathcal K\), a finite net of \(\mathcal K\), and (2) imply the corresponding convergence uniformly in \(\beta\), in \(P_{S_m}\)-probability.  Apply this conclusion to the finite list of first and second moments entering \(\mathcal B_T\) and the imbalance covariance.  The full-array signal floor and the baseline Gram lower bound keep the relevant denominators separated from zero.  Continuity of inversion on the nonsingular imbalance range and continuity of the Moore--Penrose inverse on the constant-rank stratum from \(\mathrm{ass{:}oracle\text{-}rank}\) therefore yield, on events \(\mathcal R_n\) with \(P_{S_m}(\mathcal R_n)\to1\),
\[
\sup_{\beta\in\mathcal K}
\left\|\mathcal B_T(\beta)-\mathcal B_\infty(\beta)\right\|
+
\sup_{\beta\in\mathcal K}
\left\|G_T(\beta)-G_\infty(\beta)\right\|
\longrightarrow0.
\tag{3}
\]
This argument uses only \(N\to\infty\), not \(m/n\to0\).

Consider now arbitrary deterministic sequences \(T_j\in\mathcal R_{n_j}\), \(\beta_j\in\mathcal K\), and \(H_j\in\mathcal H_{T_j}\).  Compactness of \(\mathcal K\) and of
\[
\{0\}\cup\{H\in\mathbb S_+^{Fp}:\operatorname{tr}(H)=1\}
\tag{4}
\]
gives a subsequence on which \(\beta_j\to\beta_\star\) and \(H_j\to H_\star\).  Positive congruence under the nonsingular imbalance standardization preserves positive semidefiniteness, and multiplying a score matrix by a positive scalar does not change its lower-tail rule.  We therefore use the standardized coordinates of \(\mathrm{thm{:}oracle\text{-}deletion\text{-}loss}\) and retain the notation \(H_j\) for the congruently transformed score.

Let
\[
U_j=\sqrt N\left(\widetilde{\boldsymbol\tau}^{\,\mu}_{T_j}
-\boldsymbol\tau_{T_j}^{\mu}\right),
\qquad
\widetilde{\boldsymbol\tau}^{\,\mu}_{T_j}
=\frac1N\sum_{i\in T_j}\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}
Qw_q\mathbf 1\{Z_i=q\}\mu_{iq}(\beta_j),
\tag{5}
\]
and let \(Z_j\) denote the standardized vector \(\sqrt N\Delta_{T_j}\).  The boundedness in (1) makes the maximum influence in \(\mathrm{lem{:}balanced\text{-}random\text{-}partition\text{-}clt}\) negligible.  The moment convergence in (2)--(3) and that lemma give joint convergence, including convergence of second moments,
\[
(U_j,Z_j)\ \Rightarrow\
(\mathcal B_\infty(\beta_\star)Z+R,Z),
\qquad
Z\sim N(0,I_{Fp}),
\tag{6}
\]
where \(R\) is centered Gaussian and \(\operatorname{Cov}(R,Z)=0\).  Hence \(R\) and \(Z\) are independent.

Let \(b_j=a_{T_j,H_j}\).  If \(H_\star\neq0\), orthogonal diagonalization writes
\(Z^{\mathsf T}H_\star Z=\sum_{\ell=1}^{d_\star}\lambda_\ell Z_\ell^2\) with \(d_\star\geq1\) and \(\lambda_\ell>0\).  The first summand has a density on \((0,\infty)\), convolution with the remaining independent summands preserves absence of atoms, and the Gaussian vector lies in the null space with probability zero.  Thus this quadratic form has a continuous distribution, so convergence in (6), convergence of the score matrices, and the quantile characterization of an exact lower-tail rule show that
\[
b_j\ \longrightarrow\
b_{H_\star}(Z)
=\mathbf 1\{Z^{\mathsf T}H_\star Z\leq q_{H_\star}\}
\quad\text{in distribution},
\qquad
E b_{H_\star}(Z)=\alpha.
\tag{7}
\]
The choice of strict or weak inequality is immaterial because the Gaussian boundary has probability zero.  If \(H_\star=0\), (4) implies that \(H_j=0\) eventually, and exact common boundary randomization gives \(b_j\equiv\alpha\); in this case define \(b_{H_\star}\equiv\alpha\).  Thus in both cases \(0\leq b_{H_\star}\leq1\), \(E b_{H_\star}=\alpha\), and \(b_{H_\star}(-z)=b_{H_\star}(z)\).

We next verify that exact unequal inclusions do not survive this limit.  Under balanced complete randomization,
\[
\pi_{iq}(T,H)
=\frac1Q\left[
\eta+\frac{1-\eta}{\alpha}
E_{\mathrm{CR}}\{a_{T,H}\mid Z_i=q\}
\right].
\tag{8}
\]
There is an explicit coupling of the conditional and unconditional complete randomizations: if the unconditional label of unit \(i\) is not \(q\), interchange it with a uniformly selected unit having label \(q\); otherwise do nothing.  Counting preimages shows that the resulting assignment is uniform conditional on \(Z_i=q\).  The interchange changes every standardized sum in (6) by at most \(C/\sqrt N\), uniformly in \(i\) and \(q\), because the arrays in (1) and the baselines are bounded.  Applying (7) under this coupling, and using zero Gaussian boundary mass when \(H_\star\neq0\), yields
\[
\max_{i\in T_j,q\in\mathcal Q}
\left|E_{\mathrm{CR}}(b_j\mid Z_i=q)-\alpha\right|
\longrightarrow0.
\tag{9}
\]
For \(H_j=0\) the equality in (9) is exact.  The same argument applies to \(G_{T_j}(\beta_j)\), because (3), positive rank, and \(\mathrm{lem{:}gaussian\text{-}boundary\text{-}regularity}\) give a nonconstant limiting quadratic form with zero boundary mass.  Consequently, by (8),
\[
\max_{i,q}\left|pi_{iq}(T_j,H_j)-\frac1Q\right|
+
\max_{i,q}\left|pi_{iq}\{T_j,G_{T_j}(\beta_j)\}-\frac1Q\right|
\longrightarrow0.
\tag{10}
\]
This is the promised leave-one-unit inclusion convergence.  The preceding subsequence proof also proves its uniform sequential form: a failure would itself supply sequences \(T_j,\beta_j,H_j,i_j,q_j\) to which the same compactness and coupling argument applies.

The likelihood ratio of the exact mixture relative to complete randomization is
\[
\ell_{T,H}=\eta+\frac{1-\eta}{\alpha}a_{T,H},
\qquad
\eta\leq\ell_{T,H}\leq \eta+\frac{1-\eta}{\alpha}.
\tag{11}
\]
It follows from (6)--(7), convergence of the randomization second moments, and the bounded density (11) that quadratic moments under the mixture converge.  In particular, for the deterministic conditional-mean table,
\[
\begin{aligned}
&N\left{V_{T_j}^{\mu}(H_j,\beta_j)
-V_{T_j}^{\mu}(G_{T_j}(\beta_j),\beta_j)\right}\\
&\quad\longrightarrow
\frac{1-\eta}{\alpha}\operatorname{tr}(M_{\beta_\star})
E\!\left[g_{\beta_\star}(Z)
\{b_{H_\star}(Z)-b_{G_\star}(Z)\}\right],
\tag{12}
\end{aligned}
\]
where
\[
b_{G_\star}(Z)
=\mathbf 1\{g_{\beta_\star}(Z)\leq q_{\alpha,\beta_\star}\}.
\tag{13}
\]
To justify (12) explicitly, exact mass \(E b_{H_\star}=E b_{G_\star}=\alpha\) makes the \(R^{\mathsf T}WR\) terms equal, independence and centering make both cross terms zero, and
\[
Z^{\mathsf T}M_{\beta_\star}Z
=\operatorname{tr}(M_{\beta_\star})g_{\beta_\star}(Z)
\tag{14}
\]
is the remaining explained loss.  The ordinary statistic in (5) can be replaced by the exact-inclusion Horvitz--Thompson statistic in (12): by (10), its coefficient difference is uniformly \(o(1)\); the balanced complete-randomization covariance identity and the density bound (11) make the centered squared difference \(o(N^{-1})\).  Its mean is also \(o(N^{-1/2})\), because the limit in (6) is odd in \((R,Z)\) while each limiting quadratic lower-tail density is even.  Exact Horvitz--Thompson centering then makes the total squared difference \(o(N^{-1})\).

For completeness, the stochastic outcome residual has no hidden action-dependent first-order term.  Put
\(sigma_{i,qr}(\beta)=E_\beta(\varepsilon_{iq}\varepsilon_{ir}\mid x_{in})\).
Independence across units removes all \(i\neq j\) terms.  For \(q\neq r\), mutual exclusivity of labels and positivity from \(\eta>0\) give, exactly,
\[
E\left[
\left\{\frac{\mathbf 1(Z_i=q)}{\pi_{iq}}-1\right\}
\left\{\frac{\mathbf 1(Z_i=r)}{\pi_{ir}}-1\right\}
\right]=-1,
\tag{15}
\]
which is independent of the action.  The diagonal difference between \(H_j\) and \(G_{T_j}(\beta_j)\), multiplied by \(N\), is
\[
\frac1N\sum_{i\in T_j}\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}
w_q^{\mathsf T}Ww_q\,\sigma_{i,qq}(\beta_j)
\left[
\frac1{\pi_{iq}(T_j,H_j)}
-\frac1{\pi_{iq}\{T_j,G_{T_j}(\beta_j)\}}
\right],
\tag{16}
\]
and (10), the lower bound \(\pi_{iq}\geq\eta/Q\), and the uniform second-moment envelope make (16) tend to zero.

The lower-tail identity \(\mathrm{lem{:}finite\text{-}lower\text{-}tail\text{-}identity}\), applied on Gaussian space with \(L=g_{\beta_\star}(Z)\), \(a=b_{H_\star}\), and \(a_0=b_{G_\star}\), gives
\[
E\!\left[g_{\beta_\star}(Z)
\{b_{H_\star}(Z)-b_{G_\star}(Z)\}\right]
=E\!\left[(g_{\beta_\star}(Z)-q_{\alpha,\beta_\star})
\{b_{H_\star}(Z)-b_{G_\star}(Z)\}\right]
\geq0.
\tag{17}
\]
Equations (12)--(17) prove that every deterministic regular sequence \((T_j,\beta_j,H_j)\) has nonnegative limiting action regret.

It remains only to pass from sequential limits to the displayed expected infimum.  For a fixed finite \(T\), only finitely many weak score orderings of \(\Omega_T\) can be induced by quadratic forms, so the inner infimum is measurable and may be approximated by an action.  The fixed-member second-moment envelope and \(\mathrm{lem{:}uniform\text{-}single\text{-}wave\text{-}risk}\) give a constant \(C<\infty\) such that
\[
\left|N\{V_T(H,\beta)-V_T(G_T(\beta),\beta)\}\right|\leq C
\tag{18}
\]
for every \(\beta\), every \(H\), and every balanced \(T\).  If the claimed uniform lower limit failed, there would be \(\epsilon>0\), a sequence \(\beta_j\), and, after discarding the event \(\mathcal R_{n_j}^c\) using (18), regular deterministic complements \(T_j\) and actions \(H_j\) for which the left side of (12) is at most \(-\epsilon\).  Compactness would produce a further subsequence covered by (17), a contradiction.  Hence
\[
\liminf_n\inf_{\beta\in\mathcal K}
E_{S_m}\inf_{H\in\mathcal H_T}
N\{V_T(H,\beta)-V_T(G_T(\beta),\beta)\}\geq0.
\tag{19}
\]
Because \(G_T(\beta)\in\mathcal H_T\) by \(\mathrm{lem{:}oracle\text{-}action\text{-}admissible}\), every inner infimum in (19) is at most zero.  Thus (19) is equivalent to the asserted uniform convergence of its absolute value.  The boundary checks are exact: choosing \(H=G_T(\beta)\) gives zero at every finite \(N\), whereas \(H=0\) has the strictly positive Gaussian oracle-gain limit.  Finite-lattice negative regrets are not ruled out; (19) shows precisely that they vanish after first-order scaling.
added_lemmas.justification: The proposition proves that the empirical Gaussian oracle is first-order optimal even against arbitrary exact finite-score actions.
added_lemmas.gap: It supplies no quantitative remainder at the square-root-pilot scale.
added_lemmas.consumer: It provides the action-loss lower comparison needed to exclude macroscopic pilot fractions.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every fixed member of \(\mathfrak M\) and every admissible balanced pilot-size sequence \(m=m(n)\in\mathcal M_n\) such that \(m/n\to c\) for some \(c\in(0,1)\),
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}n^{3/2}\mathcal E_n(m)=\infty.
\]
The lower bound is uniform over \(\beta\in\mathcal K\) for the fixed member, but no common numerical bound over all members of \(\mathfrak M\) is asserted.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix a member of \(\mathfrak M\) and let
\[
a_-=\inf_{\beta\in\mathcal K}a(\beta)>0,
\tag{20}
\]
whose positivity is part of \(\mathrm{thm{:}oracle\text{-}deletion\text{-}loss}\).  Define
\[
q_n(\beta)=E_{S_m}\inf_{H\in\mathcal H_T}
N\{V_T(H,\beta)-V_T(G_T(\beta),\beta)\},
\qquad T=T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}.
\tag{21}
\]
The first-order arbitrary-action proposition gives a deterministic sequence \(\epsilon_n\downarrow0\), depending on the fixed member, such that
\[
\inf_{\beta\in\mathcal K}q_n(\beta)\geq-\epsilon_n.
\tag{22}
\]

For a pilot-measurable rule \(\delta_m\), condition on \(S_m\) and the pilot information.  By the stable product law, the main-wave potential outcomes are conditionally independent of the pilot outcomes.  Hence the realized action \(H=\delta_m\) is one of the actions over which the infimum in (21) is taken, and
\[
nL_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta)
\geq \frac Nn q_n(\beta)
\geq-\frac Nn\epsilon_n.
\tag{23}
\]
The exact risk reduction \(\mathrm{prop{:}second\text{-}order\text{-}risk\text{-}reduction}\) gives
\[
n\{R_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta)-R_n^{\mathrm{or}}(\beta)\}
=nD_{n,m}(\beta)+nL_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta).
\tag{24}
\]
Since \(m/n\to c\in(0,1)\), the macroscopic conclusion of \(\mathrm{thm{:}oracle\text{-}deletion\text{-}loss}\) yields
\[
\sup_{\beta\in\mathcal K}
|nD_{n,m}(\beta)-c\,a(\beta)|\longrightarrow0.
\tag{25}
\]
Combining (20)--(25), for all sufficiently large \(n\), every pilot rule and every \(\beta\in\mathcal K\) satisfy
\[
R_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta)-R_n^{\mathrm{or}}(\beta)
\geq \frac{c a_-}{2n}>0.
\tag{26}
\]
Taking the positive part, the supremum over \(\beta\), and then the infimum over \(\delta_m\) gives
\[
\mathcal E_n(m)\geq\frac{c a_-}{2n}.
\tag{27}
\]
Multiplication by \(n^{3/2}\) proves the assertion.
added_lemmas.justification: The deletion gain is order \(n^{-1}\) for a positive pilot fraction and no arbitrary main-wave action can offset it at first order.
added_lemmas.gap: The bounded-pilot and the two sublinear interior endpoint windows remain open.
added_lemmas.consumer: It rules out every fixed positive pilot fraction while preserving the open square-root-scale question.

proposed.statement:
For every fixed member of \(\mathfrak M\) and every admissible balanced pilot-size sequence \(m=m(n)\in\mathcal M_n\) with \(N=n-m=o(n)\),
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}n^{3/2}\mathcal E_n(m)=\infty.
\]
No conclusion is asserted here for bounded \(m\), for \(m=o(\sqrt n)\), for \(\sqrt n=o(m)=o(n)\), or for a positive pilot fraction with \(N\asymp n\).
proposed.justification: The lemma excludes a sublinear main wave using a first-order arbitrary-action comparison when the main wave diverges and exact risk domination when it stays bounded.
proposed.gap: Bounded pilots, diverging pilots with \(m=o(\sqrt n)\), and the large-interior window \(\sqrt n=o(m)=o(n)\) remain open; a separate lemma now excludes positive pilot fractions.
proposed.consumer: Together with the positive-fraction lemma, it prevents macroscopic endpoint designs from being justified by the conditional interior envelope.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The revised proof uses the new arbitrary-action proposition on diverging main-wave subsequences and retains exact risk domination on bounded subsequences, so the dependency spine and result notes must be synchronized.

prose_updates.tldr: A balanced pilot and a positive-support exact-\(\alpha\) main-wave mixture retain exact Horvitz--Thompson centering for the realized finite-population factorial vector.  The proved contribution now includes the exact two-component risk identity, the first-order exact-mixture oracle-gain limit, and first-order Gaussian optimality of the empirical oracle against arbitrary exact finite-score actions.  Those results exclude both a fixed positive pilot fraction and a sublinear main wave.  The balanced-grid argmin proposition remains purely deterministic: compact-window second-order convergence, the pilot-information bridge, and the bounded and sublinear-interior endpoint comparisons are still open, so no square-root pilot recommendation is yet certified.

project_justification.gap: Existing factorial rerandomization theory supplies first-order Gaussian precision and existing two-wave work supplies accounting architecture, but neither proves the moving-boundary exact Horvitz--Thompson comparison at the square-root pilot scale.  The present information audit also shows that the stated moment conditions do not identify the pilot Fisher-information limit.
project_justification.niche: On a fixed complete baseline array with a full-dimensional product parameter domain, the design problem separates exactly into a deletion contrast and a potentially signed action-loss contrast.  A compactness, leave-one-unit, and Gaussian lower-tail argument now controls the latter at first order for arbitrary actions, including exact ties and unequal inclusions.
project_justification.fill: The note proves exact pooled Horvitz--Thompson accounting, the explicit first-order exact-mixture oracle-gain coefficient, first-order arbitrary-action Gaussian optimality, exclusion of fixed positive pilot fractions and sublinear main waves, the exact pilot likelihood and realized information audit, and a conditional deterministic argmin certificate.  It leaves both frontier coefficients, compact-window convergence, the information-to-action bridge, and the remaining endpoint windows as explicit open questions.

prose_updates.related_work: Han and Deng provide the closest factorial sample-splitting architecture and first-order oracle equivalence; their results inform the present first-order comparison but do not supply the deletion cancellation or exact moving-boundary action loss.  Li and Ding provide the random-partition central limit theorem used for bounded conditional-mean tables.  Li, Ding, and Rubin provide the symmetric truncated-Gaussian predecessor, while the present first-order arbitrary-action comparison additionally carries randomized ties, exact unequal inclusions, and arbitrary centered quadratic actions through a subsequence limit.  Yamin provides the deterministic compact-localization and argmin-transfer architecture, not the statistical square-root rate or its coefficients.  Armstrong's LAN efficiency bounds become relevant only after an actual pilot-information limit is available.  Horvitz and Thompson support exact inverse-inclusion centering.  Menon, Chakrabarti, and Nerella motivate sequential factorial replications, but no pilot-size recommendation is certified until the compact-window and remaining endpoint premises are proved.
prose_updates.interpretation: For planning, the proved coefficient \(a(\beta)\) quantifies the first-order loss from deleting a macroscopic fraction of units for learning.  No exact finite quadratic action can asymptotically beat the empirical Gaussian oracle at order \(N^{-1}\), even though finite-lattice action-loss contrasts may be negative.  Consequently, both fixed positive pilot fractions and designs leaving only a sublinear main wave are ruled out.  The familiar balance \(A t+B/t\) remains a conditional design calculation, not a validated sample-size rule for this experiment.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Exact score orderings can jump on deterministic lattices and exact inclusion probabilities can be unequal.  Compact action and parameter subsequences, zero Gaussian boundary mass, an explicit leave-one-unit coupling, and exact residual cancellation absorb those effects at first order and suffice for macroscopic endpoint exclusion.  They provide no quantitative remainder at scale \(n^{-3/2}\), so they do not establish the compact-window second-order premise.  Separately, smooth first and second outcome moments do not control score information as a function of the baseline, so the pilot LAN information cannot be fixed at \(I(\beta)\) without additional derivation.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Established results are exact Horvitz--Thompson centering and accounting, the one-wave risk bound, common oracle-map convergence, Gaussian boundary regularity, the first-order exact-mixture oracle gain, first-order arbitrary-action Gaussian optimality, the exact pilot likelihood and information audit, exclusion of positive pilot fractions and sublinear main waves, and the conditional deterministic envelope transfer.  The coefficient \(A\) remains an unresolved deletion candidate and \(B\) remains a Gaussian action candidate.  Uniform frontier-scale deletion, exact finite action curvature, information convergence, bounded pilots, the two sublinear-interior endpoint windows, and the unconditional global pilot rule are open.  The causal estimand remains the fixed realized factorial vector throughout.

statement_notes.justification: The lemma excludes a sublinear main wave using first-order arbitrary-action optimality for diverging main waves and exact risk domination for bounded ones.
statement_notes.gap: Bounded pilots and the two sublinear-interior pilot windows remain open; positive pilot fractions are handled by a separate proved lemma.
statement_notes.consumer: Together with the positive-fraction result, it supplies the two macroscopic endpoint exclusions needed by the conditional grid transfer.

statement_notes.justification: The proposition transfers every arbitrary exact finite quadratic action to a Gaussian mass-\(\alpha\) rule and certifies nonnegative limiting regret.
statement_notes.gap: No rate sharper than \(o(N^{-1})\) is obtained.
statement_notes.consumer: It converts the first-order deletion gain into a uniform lower bound for macroscopic pilot fractions.

statement_notes.justification: The positive deletion coefficient cannot be offset by any arbitrary main-wave action at first order.
statement_notes.gap: It does not address pilots smaller than a positive fraction.
statement_notes.consumer: It removes the fixed-positive-fraction endpoint from the unresolved global pilot question.
